question: Who wrote Pakistan: A Hard Country?
why: Anatol Lieven wrote Pakistan: A Hard Country (2011).
rel: The book looks at Pakistan's state, society, politics and security.

question: Who wrote Mein Kampf?
why: Mein Kampf was written by Adolf Hitler.
rel: It was published in two volumes in the 1920s.

question: Where do the Indus and Kabul rivers meet?
why: The Kabul River joins the Indus near Attock Khurd in Punjab.
rel: The Indus then flows south to the Arabian Sea.

question: What is evaporation?
options: Change of a vapour into a liquid
Change of a liquid into vapour from its surface
Change of a solid directly into vapour
Change of a liquid into a solid
why: Evaporation turns liquid into vapour at the surface and can happen below boiling point.
rel: Condensation is the reverse process.

question: Who captained Pakistan to the 1992 Cricket World Cup title?
why: Imran Khan led Pakistan to the 1992 World Cup title.
rel: Pakistan beat England in the final at Melbourne.

question: Where is NATO’s headquarters?
why: NATO's headquarters is in Brussels, Belgium.
rel: NATO's founding treaty dates to 4 April 1949.

question: What is a zero matrix?
options: A matrix with all diagonal elements one
A matrix with only one row
A matrix whose determinant is one
A matrix in which every element is zero
why: A zero matrix has every element equal to zero.
rel: Adding a zero matrix of the same size leaves a matrix unchanged.

question: What is the world’s largest sea?
why: The Philippine Sea is commonly cited as the largest sea (marginal sea).
rel: It lies in the western North Pacific Ocean.
problem: Ranking of seas depends on the definition used; Philippine Sea is the standard answer.

question: From whom did Pakistan purchase Gwadar?
why: Pakistan bought Gwadar from the Sultanate of Oman and took possession in 1958.
rel: Gwadar is a major CPEC port in Balochistan.

question: When were the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms enacted?
why: The Government of India Act 1919 implemented the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms.
rel: The reforms introduced dyarchy in the provinces.

question: Hazrat Muadh ibn Jabal was appointed governor/representative to which region?
why: The Prophet (PBUH) sent Muadh ibn Jabal to Yemen to teach and judge.
rel: This is a well-known report in hadith literature.

question: Which is the most developed continent?
why: Europe ranks highest on many human-development measures.
rel: The Human Development Index combines health, education and income.
problem: No single official answer; North America also ranks high. Europe chosen as standard answer.

question: Who is known by the title “Jami-ul-Quran”?
why: Uthman (RA) is called Jami-ul-Quran because he standardized and distributed copies of the Quran.
rel: Abu Bakr (RA) ordered the first collection after the Battle of Yamama.
problem: Some sources also apply the title to Abu Bakr (RA); Uthman is the common answer.

question: Who was Pakistan's second Prime Minister?
why: Nazimuddin became PM in 1951 after Liaquat Ali Khan was assassinated.
rel: He had earlier been Governor-General of Pakistan.

question: When was the Quit India Movement launched?
why: The Congress passed the Quit India resolution in Bombay on 8 August 1942.
rel: Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call.

question: Who won the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
why: France beat Croatia 4-2 in the 2018 final.
rel: Russia hosted the tournament.

question: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
why: Bishkek is the capital of Kyrgyzstan.
rel: Kyrgyzstan is landlocked and its currency is the som.

question: What was Allama Iqbal's first Persian philosophical book?
why: Asrar-e-Khudi (1915) was Iqbal's first Persian philosophical book.
rel: Bang-e-Dara (1924) was his first major Urdu collection.

question: When was the Tashkent Declaration signed?
why: The Tashkent Declaration was signed on 10 January 1966 by Shastri and Ayub Khan.
rel: It followed the 1965 Indo-Pakistani War.

question: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly?
why: Rahila Durrani was elected the first woman Speaker of the Balochistan Assembly in December 2015.
rel: She served until August 2018; Abdul Quddus Bizenjo succeeded her.

question: Complete the sentence: “Ali was born ___ 20 August 1997.”
why: Use 'on' with a specific date, for example 'on 20 August 1997'.
rel: Use 'in' with a month or year, like 'in August'.

question: Where are Pakistan's major coal reserves found?
why: Thar in Tharparkar district, Sindh, has Pakistan's largest coal resource.
rel: Coal is also found in Balochistan, Punjab and KP.

question: How is an earthquake's magnitude measured?
why: Modern earthquake magnitude is reported on the Moment Magnitude scale (Mw); Richter was the older scale.
rel: Mercalli measures intensity (effects), not magnitude.
problem: Richter scale is the traditional exam answer; Mw is the modern one.

question: What is cutting away unwanted parts of an image called?
why: Cropping removes unwanted outer parts of an image.
rel: Resizing changes dimensions, not the visible bounds.

question: When did Pakistan become a member of the UN?
why: Pakistan was admitted to the UN on 30 September 1947.
rel: It was admitted by UN General Assembly Resolution 108 (II).

question: What does SAFTA stand for?
options: South Asian Finance and Trade Association
why: SAFTA stands for South Asian Free Trade Area.
rel: It was signed in 2004 and took effect in 2006 under SAARC.

question: What is one tenth of 120?
why: One tenth of 120 is 120 / 10 = 12.
rel: One tenth means 10 percent.

question: Who produced the first complete, published Urdu translation of the Quran?
why: Shah Abdul Qadir's idiomatic Urdu translation (1790, published 1829) is commonly credited as the first complete Urdu translation.
rel: His brother Shah Rafiuddin made the first verbatim (word-by-word) Urdu translation.
problem: Disputed: Shah Rafiuddin's verbatim translation is also called first complete; Shah Abdul Qadir is the common answer.

question: In which year did World War I end?
why: World War I ended in 1918 with the Armistice on 11 November.
rel: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.

question: Who is known by the title “Ruhullah”?
why: Prophet Isa (AS) is called Ruhullah, meaning Spirit of Allah, in Islamic tradition.
rel: Musa (AS) is Kalimullah and Ibrahim (AS) is Khalilullah.

question: Which country has the world's longest written national constitution?
why: India has the longest written constitution of any sovereign country.
rel: It was adopted on 26 November 1949 and took effect on 26 January 1950.
